title: mutable local bindings execute unchanged inside a Flow
notes:
specification/durable-execution.mdx, 'Flow' (SA-2): 'Ordinary control flow — branches, loops, let bindings, closure capture, and recursion — MUST execute unchanged inside a Flow.' This case certifies the CURRENT refusal the (SA-2) marker records — 'a let binding inside a Flow body is refused VIBE4105' — as specification/index.mdx requires: a case certifying a measured gap is evidence FOR the gap, stays green, and is retired when the implementation moves, at which point this flips to expect output. Branches and loops crossed already (the withdrawn VIBE4106/4107 walls); let, capture, and recursion are the half of the sentence still refused, and each needs its own pin so the three cannot retire silently one by one.

RETIRED 2026-09-05 by the implementation lane: §Flow (SA-2) requires ordinary locals, closures, calls, recursion and computed values, not Plan projections. The executable body compiler now uses checked transitive reachability and computes values before codec validation. The reference compiles and prints the declared descriptor marker. poc/src/durable/body-compiler.test.ts additionally executes the actual non-recursive corpus sources through live and replayed requests, checking their exact inputs and outputs with one worker call. The recursive fixture itself is intentionally not invoked; the same unit suite executes terminating recursion. The previous diagnostic is retained above as history, not a language restriction.

xfail.reason: The Go backend still refuses this ordinary Flow program through its legacy Plan/capture or transitive-Manifest limitation. The reference executable-body path now implements it. This marker records a missing implementation, not permission to weaken the Flow contract.
